qs.stem: Which of the following HTML tag is used to puts a line break in the text?
qs.sol:
The HTML
tag inserts a line break in text.
qs.rel: Void (empty) elements. Neighbours: br, hr, img, input, meta, link have no closing tag; p and li may omit end tags in HTML; XHTML needs br/ and so on. Also   adds a non-breaking space.

qs.stem: Which of the following is used to create static web pages?
qs.sol:
HTML defines the structure and content of a static web page.

The other choices involve asynchronous scripting or server-side page generation.
qs.rel: Static vs dynamic pages. Neighbours: static = fixed HTML/CSS served as-is; dynamic = built at request time by ASP/PHP/JSP with a database; AJAX updates parts of a page without reload; JavaScript alone is client-side dynamic behaviour.

qs.sol: HTML uses a container element to define the list type. The ol element creates the ordered-list container, and li elements supply its individual entries. The browser then presents those entries with an ordered marker sequence.
qs.rel: Ordered list structure. Neighbours: ol numbered (type, start, reversed), ul bulleted, dl with dt/dd; li is the item tag; list-style-type values disc, circle, square, decimal, lower-roman.

qs.stem: Which of the following HTML tags is used to embed an image in an HTML page?
qs.sol: To embed an image in an HTML page, you must use the tag. This is the standard element defined in HTML5 for displaying images within a document structure.
qs.rel: Embedding images. Neighbours: img is void; attributes src, alt, width, height, usemap; background images are set via CSS; picture/figure elements are HTML5; GIF supports animation, JPEG photos, PNG transparency.

qs.stem: Which of the following elements is used to define rows of a table?
qs.sol:
The HTML tr element defines a table row; th and td define cells inside a row.

TR defines a table row.
qs.rel: Table structure. Neighbours: tr row, td data cell, th header cell, caption, thead/tbody/tfoot; colspan/rowspan merge cells; border and cellpadding/cellspacing style the table.

qs.stem: Which HTML attribute is used to define the URL of the image?
qs.sol: The src attribute of an HTML img element specifies the image URL.
qs.rel: Image attributes. Neighbours: src = path/URL, alt = alternative text, width/height, align (legacy), border (legacy), title tooltip, usemap for image maps; src can be relative or absolute path.

qs.stem: How many different levels of heading does HTML support?
qs.sol:
The levels represent the importance and structural hierarchy of the content on a webpage:

<h1> : The most important heading. It is typically used for the main title of a page. Search engines and screen readers rely on this to understand the primary topic.

<h2>  through <h6> : These are used for sub-sections. As the number increases, the visual size of the text typically decreases, and the "importance" level drops.
qs.rel: Heading levels. Neighbours: h1 biggest/most important to h6 smallest; there is no h7; headings are block elements, used by search engines for structure; use title for page title, not h1 by default.

qs.stem: Which of the following are the building blocks of HTML?
qs.sol:
HTML elements are the building blocks of an HTML document.

They define the structure and content of a web page.
qs.rel: HTML basic unit. Neighbours: element = start tag + content + end tag; attributes modify elements; tags mark them; DOM tree is built from elements; nested elements form parent-child relations.

qs.stem: HTML lets us use only ______ characters.
qs.sol:
The official paper keys ASCII. Historically HTML source was described using ASCII-compatible characters, although modern HTML supports Unicode.

The official paper keys ASCII for this historical wording.
qs.rel: Character encoding. Neighbours: ASCII 7-bit 128 characters; Unicode/UTF-8 is HTML5 default and supports all languages; meta charset declares encoding; ANSI, EBCDIC are other (IBM) codes.

qs.stem: HTML tags are element names surrounded by ______.
qs.sol:
An HTML tag encloses an element name between < and >. Those symbols are angle brackets, as in

qs.rel: Tag syntax. Neighbours: tag = name in angle brackets; end tag has slash; attributes only in start tag; tags are case-insensitive in HTML but case-sensitive in XML; comment is <!-- -->.

qs.stem: HTML links are defined with the ____ tag.
qs.sol: HTML links are defined using the anchor tag <a>. This element requires an href attribute to specify the destination URL for the hyperlink connection.
qs.rel: Hyperlinks. Neighbours: a href creates link, a name/id creates anchor; target attribute (_blank, _self); mailto: and tel: links; link tag in head is for stylesheets, not clickable links.

qs.stem: How many forms can we have on a webpage at the maximum?
qs.sol: HTML standards do not impose a specific numerical cap on the number of form elements within a single document. While practical performance constraints might exist in browsers, the specification allows for multiple forms without restriction.
qs.rel: Forms per page. Neighbours: multiple forms allowed but forms cannot be nested; each has its own action/method; GET vs POST; inputs outside form need form attribute to submit.

qs.stem: When was HTML 5 released?
qs.sol:
HTML5 became a W3C Recommendation in 2014, the release date used by the official key.

HTML5 reached W3C Recommendation status in 2014.
qs.rel: HTML versions. Neighbours: HTML 2.0 (1995), 3.2 (1997), 4.01 (1999), XHTML 1.0 (2000), HTML5 (W3C Recommendation Oct 2014); HTML5 adds audio, video, canvas, semantic tags, local storage.

qs.stem: Which of the following HTML element is used to define table data/cell?
qs.sol: The correct HTML element for defining table data cells is <td>. While <table> creates the container and <tr> defines rows, <th> is specifically for header cells. Therefore, option 1 accurately identifies the standard data cell tag.
qs.rel: Table cell tag. Neighbours: td data cell vs th header cell (bold, centred) vs tr row; colspan/rowspan; align and valign legacy attributes; headers attribute links cells for accessibility.

qs.stem: HTML attributes are always specified in the ______ tag(s).
qs.sol: HTML attributes are written inside an element’s opening or start tag, alongside the tag name. Closing tags do not carry them.
qs.rel: Attribute placement. Neighbours: attributes only in start tag as name="value"; global attributes id, class, style, title; boolean attributes like checked, disabled need no value; quote values.

qs.stem: Which of the following can be used to display black color in HTML?
qs.sol: In HTML and CSS, the RGB color model defines black as having zero intensity for all three primary colors. Therefore, the value rgb(0, 0, 0) represents pure black.
qs.rel: HTML colours. Neighbours: black = rgb(0,0,0) = #000000, white = rgb(255,255,255) = #FFFFFF, red #FF0000, green #00FF00 (CSS lime), blue #0000FF; hsl, rgba add hue and alpha transparency.

qs.stem: Which of the following form is correct to show a ‘comments’ in the HTML language?
qs.sol: The correct HTML comment syntax begins with `<!--` and ends with `-->`. Therefore the valid form is `<!-- This is a comment -->`.
qs.rel: HTML comments. Neighbours: HTML <!-- -->, CSS /* */, JS // and /* */, VBScript ' or Rem, XML <!-- -->, PHP // # /* */, SQL -- ; comments are not displayed but visible in source.

qs.stem: To control the width of a cell, spanning two or more columns, which attribute is added to <th>, <td> tags?
qs.sol:
colspan specifies how many columns a table cell occupies.

width sets a width but does not make a cell span multiple columns.
qs.rel: colspan. Neighbours: colspan merges columns in a td/th, rowspan merges rows; span is for col/colgroup; column-count in CSS is for multi-column text, not tables.

qs.stem: Which of the following HTML code snippets is used to specify the path of a GIF image is stored at?
qs.sol:
The img element uses its src attribute to specify the image file path; here it points to example.gif.

The src attribute on IMG identifies the GIF path.
qs.rel: GIF path. Neighbours: img src="path/file.gif"; relative path vs absolute URL; ../ goes up one folder; forward slashes in URLs; alt text for accessibility.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements about tag is NOT correct?

opts.A: The tag may contain the width attribute.
opts.B: The tag may contain the height attribute.
opts.C: The tag may contain both width and height attributes.
opts.D: The tag cannot contain either width attribute or height attribute.

qs.sol: The question asks for the incorrect statement about HTML tags. Width and height are valid attributes used for image sizing in standard markup. Therefore, the claim that these cannot be used is false and corresponds to option 3.
qs.rel: img sizing. Neighbours: width and height are valid on img (pixels or %); specifying both avoids layout shift; alt required for accessibility; CSS width/height override attributes.

qs.sol:

qs.sol: An HTML image map enables specific clickable areas within a single image to link to different URLs or locations. It utilizes the map and area tags to define interactive regions like rectangles or circles for user navigation, distinguishing it from standard image links.

qs.stem: What is tag in HTML?

opts.A: It contains the address of the webpage.
opts.B: It contains the number of nested tags in the page.
opts.C: It contains information about the webpage.
opts.D: It contains the number of tags in the web page.

qs.sol: An HTML tag defines an element that structures content and metadata on a webpage. Tags contain information about the page's components rather than storing addresses or counting other tags.
qs.rel: Tag definition. Neighbours: tag = keyword in angle brackets; element = tags + content; attribute = extra info in start tag; entity = &name; for reserved characters.

The HTML code “

<ABBR title="Internet Explorer">IE</ABBR>

 abbreviation of Internet Explorer” is used to:

qs.stem: Which of the following HTML tags inside <select> element defines the available options in a list?
qs.sol: Within a select element, each option element defines an available choice.
qs.rel: option tag. Neighbours: select contains option (value, selected) and optgroup; multiple attribute allows multi-choice; datalist gives suggestions; textarea for long text.

qs.stem: With reference to legacy HTML <body> attributes, which attribute specifies the colour of a hyperlink after it has been visited?
qs.sol:
Key distinction:

VLINK: sets the colour of visited links in legacy HTML.

ALINK: sets the colour of an active link while it is being selected/clicked.

LINK: sets the colour of unvisited links.

Modern HTML note: these presentational body attributes are deprecated/obsolete; CSS such as :visited should be used instead.

Final answer: VLINK

Modified from the official paper: The printed phrase “after the mouse is clicked” is ambiguous between an active and a visited hyperlink; the bank clarifies the intended visited-link state.
qs.rel: Link colours. Neighbours: body link = unvisited, vlink = visited, alink = active (being clicked), text, bgcolor, background; modern CSS uses a:link, a:visited, a:hover, a:active.

qs.stem: Which of the following usages is true with respect to frames in HTML?
qs.sol: The asterisk in the COLS value assigns the remaining frame width after the fixed 80-unit column. The printed tag misspells FRAMESET, but the paper marks this syntax.
qs.rel: Frameset. Neighbours: frameset cols="80,*" gives first column 80 px and rest to second; rows attribute splits horizontally; * remainder; % allowed; frames obsolete in HTML5, replaced by iframe/CSS.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement about HTML attributes is false?

opts.B: Attributes provide additional information about an element
opts.C: Attributes are always specified in the end tag
opts.D: Attributes usually come in name/value pairs like: name = "value"

qs.sol: HTML attributes provide additional information about elements and are always placed within the opening tag, not the end tag. Option 3 is incorrect because it claims attributes appear in the closing tag, making it the false statement.
qs.rel: Attribute placement. Neighbours: attributes belong to start tag only, name=value pairs; element can have several; global attributes; end tag never has attributes.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements with reference to HTML is FALSE?

opts.A: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language.
opts.B: HTML describes the meaning of a Web page.
opts.C: HTML consists of a series of elements.
opts.D: HTML elements tell the browser how to display the content.

qs.sol: HTML marks up the structure and content of a page. Saying it describes the page’s meaning is the false statement in the printed set.
qs.rel: HTML scope. Neighbours: HTML describes structure and presentation instructions, not computation; it is a markup language, not a programming language; semantic tags convey meaning but HTML itself is not a processing language.

qs.stem: Which of the following attributes of HTML element declares a namespace for tags used in HTML document?

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT an attribute that included by the HR tag which puts a horizontal line on the page?

qs.stem:
Which of the following statements about HTML styling and colour notation are true?

(i) The HTML style attribute is used to add styles to an element, such as colour, font, size, and more. (ii) HTML colours are specified with predefined colour names, or with RGB, HEX, HSL, RGBA, or HSLA values.
qs.sol:
Concept

HTML provides the document structure, while CSS controls presentation. The style attribute places CSS declarations directly on one HTML element, and CSS colour values can use named, hexadecimal, and functional notations.

Application

Statement (i) describes inline styling: declarations such as colour, font family, and font size may be supplied through the style attribute. Statement (ii) lists recognised colour-value forms: predefined names, HEX, RGB/RGBA, and HSL/HSLA.

Contrast

Accepting the inline-style description while excluding the colour-notation description conflicts with the supported colour-value forms. …
qs.rel: Style attribute. Neighbours: style="color:red; font-size:12px" inline CSS; colours as names, RGB, HEX, HSL, RGBA, HSLA; style attribute has top priority vs external sheet rules.

qs.stem: Which of the following tag of HTML language is a container for the tags that contain information about the page?
qs.sol: The `<head>` tag contains metadata and other tags that provide information about the web page.
qs.rel: head element. Neighbours: head holds title, meta, link, style, script, base; body holds visible content; html root; DOCTYPE precedes html; meta charset and viewport.

qs.stem: In which of the following forms the EM element of emphasising text in HTML displays the emphasised text?
qs.sol:
The em element gives semantic emphasis and is normally rendered in italic type by browsers.

Italic is the default visual rendering of em.
qs.rel: em rendering. Neighbours: em renders italic (emphasis), strong bold, mark highlight, small smaller text, sub/sup scripts, del strikethrough, ins underline.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements about HTML Attributes is FALSE?

opts.A: All HTML elements cannot have attributes.
opts.B: Attributes provide additional information about elements.
opts.C: Attributes are always specified in the start tag.
opts.D: Attributes usually come in name/value pairs like: name="value".

qs.rel: Attributes. Neighbours: most elements accept attributes; attribute in start tag; name=value; global attributes apply to all elements; boolean attributes.

qs.stem: Which attribute in HTML table tag defines the number of columns in a column group?

qs.rel: col span. Neighbours: span in col/colgroup defines number of columns; colspan in td/th merges cells; colgroup allows column styling; width on col.

The base element sets the base URL and optional default target used by relative links in the document.

qs.rel: base element. Neighbours: base href sets default URL for relative links and target sets default window; only one per document, in head; meta, link, style, script, title are other head elements.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding <title> tag in HTML?
 Statements:
 I. This tag always goes outside to the <head> tag.
 II. This tag is used to indicate the title of the webpage.
 III. It is also used by search engines.
qs.sol:
The <title> tag must be placed inside the <head> section, not outside.

It defines the title of the webpage displayed in browser tabs.

Additionally, search engines use this tag for indexing and displaying results.
qs.rel: title tag. Neighbours: title is inside head, shown in browser tab/bookmarks and used by search engines; only one per page; h1 is a visible heading.

qs.stem:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
 i) Class is one of the HTML global attributes which specifies one or more class names for an element (refers to a class in a style sheet).
 ii) HTML is a markup language used for server-side processing.
 iii) CSS describes how HTML elements are to be displayed on screen, paper, or in other media.
qs.sol:
Concept: HTML is a markup language that describes document structure; a browser parses that structure, while server-side processing requires executable application logic. An HTML class is a global attribute whose tokens can be targeted by CSS selectors. CSS rules control presentation, including media-specific rendering.

For i, inspect the class attribute: it accepts one or more class tokens on an element, and selectors can use those tokens. Therefore i is true.

For ii, distinguish generating an HTML document on a server from executing logic in HTML itself. A server can produce HTML, but HTML is markup rather than a server-side processing language. Therefore ii is false. …
qs.rel: Class and CSS. Neighbours: class is a global attribute (multiple names allowed; selector .name), id unique (#name); HTML is client-side markup, not server-side; CSS controls display for screen, paper, media.

`. **Attributes** are name="value" pairs, always in the **start tag**; **global attributes**: `id` (unique), `class`, `style`, `title`, `lang`, `hidden`, `tabindex`, `contenteditable`, `data-*`. - **Document skeleton:** `` (not a tag; selects HTML5 mode) -> `` -> `` (metadata: ``, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport">`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href>`, `<style>`, `<script>`, `<base href target>`) -> `<body>`. `<title>` is inside head; shown on the tab and used by search engines. - **Text tags:** `<h1>`-`<h6>` (6 levels, h1 largest), `<p>`, `<br>`, `<hr>`, `<pre>` (preserves spaces), `<b>`/`<strong>` (bold/important), `<i>`/`<em>` (italic/emphasis), `<u>`, `<mark>`, `<small>`, `<del>`, `<ins>`, `<sub>` (H<sub>2</sub>O), `<sup>`, `<q>`, `<blockquote>`, `<code>`, `<abbr title>`, `<address>`, `<cite>`. - **Links & media:** `<a href="url" target="_blank">`; `target` values `_self _blank _parent _top`; `href="#id"` jumps within page; `mailto:` opens mail client. `<img src alt width height>` - `alt` is fallback/accessibility text; HTML5 adds `<audio controls>`, `<video controls>`, `<source>`, `<canvas>`, `<svg>`; `<iframe src>` embeds a page. **Image map:** `<img usemap="#m">` + `<map name="m">` + `<area shape="rect|circle|poly" coords href>`. - **Lists:** `<ul>` (bullets), `<ol>` (numbers; `type="1|A|a|I|i"`, `start`, `reversed`), `<li>`, `<dl>` + `<dt>` term + `<dd>` description. Nested lists go inside `<li>`. - **Tables:** `<table border>`, `<caption>`, `<thead> <tbody> <tfoot>`, `<tr>` row, `<th>` header cell (bold, centred), `<td>` data cell; `colspan` merges columns, `rowspan` merges rows; `<colgroup><col span="2">`; legacy `cellpadding` (inside cell) and `cellspacing` (between cells). - **Forms:** `<form action method="get|post">`. GET appends data to URL (visible, length-limited, bookmarkable); POST sends in body (hidden, larger). Controls: `<input type>` = text, password, email, number, date, range, color, file, hidden, radio (same `name` = one choice), checkbox, submit, reset, button, image; `<textarea rows cols>`, `<select><optgroup><option selected>`, `<label for>`, `<fieldset><legend>`, `<button>`. Attributes: `required, placeholder, maxlength, min, max, pattern, readonly, disabled, autofocus`. - **Semantic HTML5:** `<header> <nav> <main> <section> <article> <aside> <footer> <figure><figcaption>`. Deprecated/removed: `<font> <center> <marquee> <frame> <frameset> <applet> <acronym> <big> <strike>`. - **Legacy `<body>` attributes:** `bgcolor`, `text`, `link` (unvisited), `vlink` (visited), `alink` (active), `background`. Frames: `<frameset cols="80,*">` - `*` takes the rest; `<frame src>`; `<noframes>`. - **Colours:** names (`red`), hex `#RRGGBB` (`#000000` black, `#FFFFFF` white, `#FF0000` red), `rgb(0,0,0)`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()`. **Entities:** `< > & "   ©`. **Comment:** `<!-- text -->`. - **Character sets:** ASCII is 7-bit (128 characters); UTF-8 (Unicode) is the HTML5 default. Block elements (div, p, h1, ul) start on a new line; inline elements (span, a, b, img) flow in a line. `<div>` = block container, `<span>` = inline container. - **Misc:** file ext `.html/.htm`; HTML is case-insensitive and forgiving of missing close tags; XHTML is strict (lowercase, all tags closed, quoted attributes). - **Likely question angles:** (1) Tag for numbered list starting at 5 (`<ol start="5">`). (2) Output of `<p>H<sub>2</sub>O</p>` or `x<sup>2</sup>`. (3) `<b>` vs `<strong>`, `<i>` vs `<em>`. (4) cellpadding vs cellspacing; colspan vs rowspan. (5) GET vs POST. (6) Which `target` opens a new tab? (7) Which input type is NOT valid (`source`, `text-area`)? (8) Which attribute makes a field mandatory (`required`)? (9) Which tag is void (`br`, `hr`, `img`)? (10) Identify a semantic HTML5 tag (`nav`, `footer`) or an obsolete tag (`center`, `font`).

topics.title: 2. CSS — Styles, Selectors, Box Model, Properties
topics.theory:
- **Three ways to apply CSS:** **Inline** (`style` attribute), **Internal** (`<style>` in `<head>`), **External** (`<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="x.css">` — change one file to restyle the whole site). "Out-line style" is not a method. `link` attributes: rel, type, href (**not `ref`**).
- **Box model (inside → out):** **Content**, Padding, Border, Margin. `margin` shorthand sets all four sides in one declaration.
- **Properties:** `word-spacing` (space between words), `font-weight` (boldness), `font-variant` (small-caps), `font-style`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `text-decoration` values: underline, **overline**, line-through, none; `background-color` accepts colour name, hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl().
- **Selectors:** type/element (`p`), class (`.x`), id (`#x`), universal (`*`), grouping (list). 
- **Responsive web design** = HTML + CSS that automatically resizes a site for all devices. **Bootstrap** = most popular CSS framework for responsive, mobile-first sites; Tailwind CSS = utility-first framework.
- **Colour:** hsl hue 0–360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue).

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a way to apply CSS to the HTML document?
qs.sol:
CSS can be applied with an internal style block, an external stylesheet, or inline declarations.

“Out-line style” is not one of these application methods.
qs.rel: CSS application methods. Neighbours: inline, internal (style tag), external (link rel=stylesheet), @import; scripts or XML are not CSS methods; external is best for multi-page consistency.

qs.rel: CSS text spacing. Neighbours: word-spacing (gaps between words), letter-spacing (between characters), line-height, text-indent, text-align, white-space; units px, em, rem, %.

topics.deep:
- **CSS** = Cascading Style Sheets; separates presentation from HTML structure; a rule = `selector { property: value; }` (declaration block of semicolon-separated declarations). Comment: `/* text */`.
- **Three ways to apply:** (1) **Inline** - `style="..."` attribute on one element (highest priority); (2) **Internal** - `<style>` block in `<head>` (one page); (3) **External** - separate `.css` file linked via `<link rel="stylesheet" href="a.css">` (one file restyles whole site; best for maintenance). `@import url()` is another way. A `<script>` is not a way to apply CSS. `!important` beats normal declarations.
- **Cascade & specificity:** order of precedence = importance, specificity, source order. Specificity weights: inline 1000, id 100, class/attribute/pseudo-class 10, element/pseudo-element 1; universal `*` = 0.
- **Selectors:** type/element `p`, class `.note`, id `#top`, universal `*`, group `h1, h2`, descendant `div p`, child `div > p`, adjacent sibling `h1 + p`, general sibling `h1 ~ p`, attribute `a[target="_blank"]`, pseudo-classes `:hover :active :visited :link :focus :first-child :nth-child(2) :not()`, pseudo-elements `::before ::after ::first-line ::first-letter`. Link order mnemonic: **LoVe HAte** (link, visited, hover, active).
- **Box model (inside out):** **content** -> **padding** -> **border** -> **margin**. `width` applies to content by default (`box-sizing: content-box`); `border-box` includes padding+border. Margin/padding shorthand: 1 value = all; 2 = top/bottom, left/right; 3 = top, left/right, bottom; 4 = **top right bottom left** (clockwise). Vertical margins of adjacent blocks **collapse**. Padding is inside the border and shows the background; margin is transparent.
- **Colour:** names, `#RRGGBB`, `#RGB` shorthand, `rgb(r,g,b)` 0-255, `rgba(...,a)`, `hsl(hue, sat%, light%)` with **hue 0-360 degrees** (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue), `hsla`. No binary notation. `transparent`, `currentColor`.
- **Background:** `background-color`, `-image: url()`, `-repeat` (repeat, no-repeat, repeat-x), `-position`, `-size` (cover, contain), `-attachment` (fixed, scroll).
- **Text:** `color`, `text-align` (left, right, center, justify), `text-decoration` (none, underline, overline, line-through), `text-transform` (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize), `text-indent`, `letter-spacing`, **`word-spacing`** (space between words), `line-height`, `white-space`, `text-shadow`.
- **Font:** `font-family` (list with generic fallback: serif, sans-serif, monospace), `font-size`, **`font-weight`** (normal, bold, 100-900), `font-style` (normal, italic, oblique), **`font-variant`** (normal, small-caps), shorthand `font: italic bold 12px/30px Arial`.
- **Units:** absolute `px, pt, cm, mm, in, pc`; relative `em` (font size of element/parent), `rem` (root), `%`, `vw`, `vh`. **Display:** `block, inline, inline-block, none` (removed from layout) vs `visibility:hidden` (space kept). **Position:** static (default), relative, absolute, fixed, sticky; `z-index`. **Float/clear**, **Flexbox** (`display:flex; justify-content; align-items; flex-direction`), **Grid** (`display:grid; grid-template-columns`).
- **Lists/tables:** `list-style` shorthand = type + position + image; `border-collapse: collapse`; `border: 1px solid black` (width style colour). `overflow: visible|hidden|scroll|auto`. `opacity: 0-1`. `cursor: pointer`.
- **Responsive & frameworks:** media query `@media (max-width: 600px) {...}`; `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`. **Bootstrap** (12-column grid, mobile-first, most popular); Tailwind = utility-first; Foundation, Bulma also exist. CSS3 adds rounded corners (`border-radius`), shadows, gradients, transitions, animations (`@keyframes`).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) `margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px` - which side gets what? (2) Order of box-model layers. (3) Specificity: which colour wins for id vs class vs element? (4) `display:none` vs `visibility:hidden`. (5) Identify `a:hover`, `p > span`, `#id`, `.class`. (6) Invalid value for `text-align`/`font-style`. (7) Effect of `text-transform: capitalize`. (8) Hue 120 in HSL is green. (9) Which `position` value is relative to the viewport (`fixed`)? (10) External vs internal vs inline CSS advantages.

topics.title: 3. JavaScript, DOM & jQuery
topics.theory:
- **JavaScript:** client-side scripting; extension **`.js`**; embedded with **`<script>` … `</script>`** (head or body, **unlimited** scripts); accepts **single, double and backtick quotes**; can change HTML content, attributes and **CSS styles**, hide/show elements; defines **behaviour/interactivity** (events). Web scripting = creating and embedding scripts in pages.
- **String + number:** `"Volvo"+16+4` = **"Volvo164"** (left-to-right concatenation); `16+4+"Volvo"` = "20Volvo".
- **DOM:** objects with properties, methods, events; **window** = top-level browser object (master container); **document** = holds the page content; `location` = URL; `alert()` shows dialog. **Methods = actions** performed on objects; properties = values.
- **Callback function** = function passed into another function as argument. **`instanceof`** → true if object is an instance of a type. **`for…in`** iterates object property keys. `event.preventDefault()` stops default action (e.g., form submit). `Object.defineProperty` with writable:false blocks assignment.
- **Events:** onchange, onmouseover, onkeydown, onload (page finished loading), onclick, onsubmit — events give a **dynamic** interface.
- **jQuery:** `hide()` and `show()` methods; `$("p").hide()`. DHTML = **Dynamic** HTML (HTML + CSS + JavaScript + DOM), not a language.

What is/are the purpose(s) of JavaScript events?

qs.stem: Which object holds the real content of the page in JavaScript?

topics.deep:
- **JavaScript** = lightweight, interpreted, **client-side scripting** language adding behaviour/interactivity (HTML = structure, CSS = style, JS = behaviour); case-sensitive; created by Brendan Eich (Netscape, 1995); standard = **ECMAScript**; not the same as Java. File ext `.js`. Embed with `<script>...</script>` (head, body or both; no limit on number of scripts) or `<script src="a.js"></script>`. Writing/embedding scripts is called **scripting**.
- **Variables:** `var` (function scope, hoisted), `let` (block scope), `const` (block scope, cannot be reassigned). Names start with letter, `_` or `$`. **Data types:** primitive - Number, String, Boolean, Undefined, Null, BigInt, Symbol; non-primitive - Object (Array, Function, Date). Strings take `'single'`, `"double"` or backtick quotes.
- **Operators:** arithmetic `+ - * / % **`; assignment `= += -=`; comparison `==` (loose, converts type) vs `===` (strict, type + value); logical `&& || !`; `typeof`; `instanceof` returns **true/false (Boolean)**; ternary `c ? a : b`; `++ --`.
- **Type-coercion outputs:** `"Volvo"+16+4` -> `Volvo164`; `16+4+"Volvo"` -> `20Volvo`; `"5"+3` -> `53`; `"5"-3` -> `2`; `"5"*"2"` -> `10`; `5=="5"` true, `5==="5"` false; `typeof null` -> `object`; `typeof undefined` -> `undefined`; `typeof NaN` -> `number`; `0.1+0.2` -> `0.30000000000000004`.
- **Control & loops:** `if/else`, `switch` (needs `break`), `for`, `while`, `do-while` (runs at least once), `for...in` (keys of an object), `for...of` (values of an iterable), `break`, `continue`. Sequence = statements run in written order, once each; selection = if/switch; repetition = loops.
- **Functions:** `function f(a,b){return a+b;}`; function expression; arrow `(a,b)=>a+b`; a **callback** is a function passed as an argument to another function; closures; `return` ends a function.
- **Objects/Arrays:** `let o={name:"A",age:3}; o.name; o["age"]`; methods are functions stored as properties (actions performed on objects); `Object.defineProperty(o,'age',{value:25,writable:false})` makes assignment silently ignored (non-strict) so value stays 25. Array: `push, pop, shift, unshift, slice, splice, join, length, indexOf, map, filter`. String: `length, toUpperCase, substring, indexOf, charAt, split, replace`. `Math.round/floor/ceil/random/max`.
- **Popup boxes (window methods):** `alert(msg)` (OK only), `confirm(msg)` (OK/Cancel -> true/false), `prompt(msg, default)` (returns entered text or null). `document.write()` outputs into page; `console.log()` to console.
- **BOM (browser objects):** `window` (global/master container, represents the browser window), `screen`, `location` (URL, `href`, `reload()`), `history` (`back()`, `forward()`), `navigator` (browser info), `document`, timers `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`.
- **DOM:** tree of nodes; `document` object holds the page content. Parts: **Core, HTML, XML** DOM. Access: `getElementById, getElementsByClassName, getElementsByTagName, querySelector, querySelectorAll`. Change: `innerHTML, textContent, style.color, setAttribute, createElement, appendChild, removeChild`. JS can change HTML content, attributes, CSS styles, hide/show elements, validate forms.
- **Events:** `onclick, ondblclick, onmouseover, onmouseout, onkeydown, onkeyup, onload (page loaded), onchange (element value changed), onfocus, onblur, onsubmit, onresize`. `addEventListener('click', fn)`. `event.preventDefault()` cancels the default action (e.g., form submit); `stopPropagation()` stops bubbling.
- **jQuery:** library (`$` = jQuery) - `$("#id")`, `$(".c")`, `$("p")`; `hide()`, `show()`, `toggle()`, `fadeIn()`, `slideUp()`, `css()`, `html()`, `text()`, `val()`, `$(document).ready(fn)`, `$.ajax()`. **AJAX** = Asynchronous JavaScript And XML - updates part of a page without reload (XMLHttpRequest / fetch).
- **Likely question angles:** (1) Output of `var a = 5 + "5" - 2;` (55-2 = 53). (2) `typeof` of various values. (3) `==` vs `===` (`0=="0"` true, `null==undefined` true, `null===undefined` false). (4) Which loop runs at least once? (5) var/let/const differences. (6) Which box returns a value (prompt/confirm)? (7) Match event to description (onclick, onblur). (8) Which jQuery method toggles visibility? (9) Output of `for(i=0;i<3;i++) document.write(i)` -> 012. (10) `parseInt("12px")` -> 12; what is NaN.

topics.title: 4. XML
topics.theory:
- **XML** = eXtensible Markup Language; user-defined tags; used to represent and **exchange structured data between systems**; case-sensitive.
- **Rules:** every element needs a closing tag, **proper nesting**, attribute values **quoted**, **tag names are case-sensitive** (`<Markup></markup>` is invalid), one root element; names **cannot start with a digit or the letters "xml"** and cannot contain spaces. Comments `<!-- … -->` (single or multi-line). **Declaration:** `<?xml version="1.0" standalone="yes"?>`. Empty element: `<tag />`. Escape `<` as **`<`**, `>` as `>`, `&` as `&`.
- **DTD vs XML Schema:** DTD (from SGML) has **no data types**; **XML Schema defines datatypes** for elements/attributes and is written in XML. DTD `<!ELEMENT note (message)>` → child "message" occurs **exactly once** (`+` one or more, `*` zero or more, `?` optional).

qs.sol: XML represents content with nested element tags, optional attributes on elements, and permitted comments. These are syntactic components of an XML document.
qs.rel: XML syntax elements. Neighbours: XML has elements, attributes, comments <!-- -->, CDATA, processing instructions, declaration; one root element; tags are user-defined and case-sensitive.

qs.sol: XML represents structured data with user-defined tags. A sender can serialize fields into an XML document, and a receiving system can parse those tags without sharing the same programming language or platform. This makes representation and exchange between systems the practical use described.
qs.rel: XML for data exchange. Neighbours: XML is platform and language independent, self-describing, text based; used for data interchange, RSS, SOAP, config; JSON is a lighter alternative.
